key_insight: The paper reframes phase-field fracture in composite shells as a certified, replaceable constitutive operator that separates fiber, inter-fiber, and interaction damage channels via invariant-based kinematics.
engineering_relevance: This enables more flexible and verifiable shell fracture simulations for curved fiber-reinforced structures, including accurate plane-stress condensation and mechanism-specific degradation.
method: Pulls Green-Lagrange strain through the shell metric Cholesky factor and decomposes it into four orthogonal invariants with exact closure.
Uses channel-wise potentials, tension-compression split, and degradation rules to build stress, tangent, and plane-stress condensation operators.
Introduces six admissibility conditions and a three-tier certification protocol for algebra, solver state, and training-data admission.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the discretization on notched IM7/8552 shell examples in thin and curved regimes, showing curvature-driven through-thickness asymmetry and strong sensitivity to fiber orientation.
watch_item: Because the framework depends on certified operator admissibility and positive residual stiffness for regular condensation, implementation errors or poorly conditioned learned operators could compromise robustness.
paper_title: Mechanism-resolved phase-field fracture of composite shells with a certified admissible constitutive operator
